best_idea: Keep the server's timers in one queue ordered by (time, insertion sequence), and run each effect at its own scheduled time, not whenever the loop happens to poll, so the same inputs always give the same order.
decision_why: Keep the time-ordered queue and the own-time rule, add an insertion-sequence tie-break and drop the unordered change set; replace the donor's wall-clock driver with the server tick counter, since the donor has no tie-break and its change order depends on std::hash<std::string>.
acceptance: A server test schedules a DoT tick and a cooldown end at the same millisecond and asserts they run in insertion order on every run; a repeat whose next time is not later than its own is refused; one tick runs every due timer and each effect is stamped with its scheduled time.
